My daughter is severely autistic and requires general anesthesia for dental procedures. We also drove one hour each way to the dental hospital because we trusted that they were prepared to care for her. We rearranged our entire day based on the hospital's instructions.
Instead, we were left waiting for hours with absolutely no clear timeline, no communication, and no regard for the fact that my daughter has severe autism and cannot tolerate prolonged waiting. She had been fasting since the previous evening, as instructed, meaning she went an extremely long time without food or water.
During the wait, I went to the front desk multiple times to ask when my daughter's procedure would finally take place because no one had updated us. I was told there was no estimated time, and that someone would go ask the dentist and come back with an update. No one ever returned. We were simply left sitting there. That alone confirmed how terrible the communication is at this hospital.
Rather than taking her back for the dental cleaning procedure, the dental hospital gave her what they described as half a doze of the general anesthesia simply to calm her down because they were nowhere near ready to perform the procedure. More than two hours later, the medication began wearing off. She became hungry, thirsty, frustrated, and aggressive—as anyone familiar with autism could have anticipated. We were confined to a tiny room for hours while she became increasingly distressed.
When we finally decided we had no choice but to leave, the staff suddenly began scrambling to find a dentist. Until that moment, it appeared there wasn't even a dentist available to perform the procedure. Staff members were running through the halls with walkie-talkies and even stopped us at the elevator as we were leaving, telling us, "things happen." That is not an acceptable response after making a disabled patient fast, sedating her, and leaving her waiting for hours without proper planning or communication.
The drive home was heartbreaking. We then had to endure another one-hour drive home, during which my daughter became so distressed from not having eaten or had anything to drink all day that she began physically hitting everyone in the car. The entire situation was completely avoidable. The moment we got home and she was finally able to eat and drink, she calmed down almost immediately. Her suffering today was unnecessary.
This experience showed a shocking lack of organization, communication, and respect for patients with special needs and their families. We trusted Saint Bernard Hospital with one of the most vulnerable members of our family, and they completely failed her.
To any parent of a child with special needs: stay away from Saint Bernard Hospital or their dental office and seek care elsewhere. No family should have to watch their child endure what ours did because of poor planning, disorganization, and a complete lack of communication. Based on our experience, I would never entrust my daughter to this hospital again.

reviews_highlighted.comment: I rarely leave negative reviews, but I feel compelled to share my experience, in hopes it helps others make an informed choice. During my root canal, the office used a mouthpiece that held my mouth open and constantly blew air while suctioning. I understand some offices use that technology, but for me it was extremely uncomfortable. It made my throat painfully dry, the noise was overwhelming, and after a while I started feeling panicked and claustrophobic. I’ve never experienced anything like that at another dental office. During the procedure, something appeared to go wrong. The dental assistant was still in training and seemed unsure, and the receptionist came into help. As a patient lying there, that did not inspire confidence. I was so uncomfortable, I decided not to return to that location and went to another office under the same company. Unfortunately, that experience also felt awkward and left me feeling like I’d made the wrong choice by returning. The one bright spot was Ann at the front desk. She was incredibly kind, patient, and helpful with my insurance questions. She even stepped in to help during my procedure when the assistant was still learning. Her professionalism, compassion, and customer service were outstanding, and she was truly a tremendous asset to the office. Unfortunately, my overall experience with the clinical care was so uncomfortable and disorganized that I won’t be returning. I hope the practice invests more in patient comfort, better communication, and making sure staff are fully trained and supported.

I went here for a cleaning a month and a half ago and it was the worst dentist experience I’ve had. The dentist told me I had over 12 cavities before even examining me. My last x-rays were 9 months prior and I had no cavities. I don’t know if it’s because of the AI that they use or if they’re just trying to squeeze patients for money, but this was crazy to me. They told me they wanted me to come in four more times for four rounds of fillings, totaling over $1600 WITH insurance. The best part of this interaction? The dentist fully arguing with me, saying that I must never floss and have very poor dental hygiene. I don’t think I’ve gone a day without flossing & brushing in 15+ years, which I told him and he kept arguing that I definitely don’t floss. This was such a bizarre experience. I’ve never had a dentist accuse me of not flossing before, and I’ve NEVER had a practitioner argue with me like that. Just so bizarre😭

The cleaning I got was the worst I’ve ever had— it lasted ~5 minutes and left me with bruised gums and visible plaque still on my teeth. Maybe the dentist should’ve focused on cleaning my teeth instead of asking if I was interested in whitening treatments. So frustrating as my insurance covers two cleanings a year and this 100% was a waste of that coverage.

I told them very clearly I would be going elsewhere for future care because (1) their cost estimates are insane, (2) I truly cannot believe that I developed 12+ cavities in 9 months, and (3) the cleaning I received was shoddy at best.

I was going to let it go and not leave a harsh review, until I got a text recently. Over a month and a half after my visit, they contacted me saying that (without my consent) they contacted my insurance to ask for a pre authorization on the fillings that they previously suggested. I told them in no uncertain terms that I would not be coming back and I recall explicitly telling the receptionist to please make a copy of my x-rays to forward to my next dentist. I don’t know why they went behind my back to try to get me to return to their clinic— maybe they have a quota to fill. But I will definitely not be returning. Please avoid this place!! Trust the recent reviews and don’t believe the AI-generated responses she posts to each honest review!
